To begin with

The general steps are in: https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/clustering-a-binary-matrix-in-r/

We are going to use the same Jaccard distances used in K-Modes.

library(e1071)
memory.limit(size=1e+13)
## Warning: 'memory.limit()' is no longer supported
## [1] Inf
rownames(myMMcondition)=1:nrow(myMMcondition)

method=“complete”. This method is also known as the diameter or maximum method. In this method, we consider the similarity of the most distant pair. That is, the distance between one cluster and another is considered equal to the greatest distance between any member of one cluster and any member of the other. It tends to produce more compact clusters. A disadvantage of this method is that outliers can cause nearby groups to merge later than is optimal.

clusters_d <- hclust(distancias, method="complete") 


cluster3 <- cutree(clusters_d, k = 3)

In this case, the “complete” linkage method was chosen, which calculates the maximum distance between the groups before merging them.

table(cluster3)
## cluster3
##     1     2     3 
## 51382   437    16

The vast majority of patients fall into a single cluster. This method is not very useful here.

table(cluster3)
## cluster3
##     1     2     3 
## 51382   437    16
table(cluster3)*100/nrow(myMMcondition)

The Rand Index (Rand, 1971) and the Adjusted Rand Index (Yeung & Ruzzo, 2001) are commonly used indices for comparing clustering results against external criteria (Hubert, 1985). (https://doi.org/10.1016/B978-0-12-381972-7.00003-8)

ARI (Adjusted Rand Index) is a corrected version of the Rand index, which measures the degree of overlap between two partitions. The Rand index presents scaling issues, prompting the proposal of a corrected version. While the Rand index ranges from 0 to 1, the ARI can take negative values ​​if the index falls below the expected index value [ 36 ]. Although the ARI can take negative values, its range is generally considered to be [0, 1]. An ARI value of 0 indicates that the actual and modeled groupings do not agree on pairings, while a value of 1 indicates that the actual and modeled groupings represent the same clusters. (https://doi.org/10.1016/bs.adcom.2021.09.008)

In general, the ARI value falls between 0 and 1. The index value equals 1 only if a partition is completely identical to the intrinsic structure, and it is close to 0 for a random partition. (https://doi.org/10.1016/B978-0-12-811654-8.00003-8)

The Rand index calculates the similarity between two clustering results by considering all points identified within the same cluster. This value is 0 when points are randomly assigned to clusters and 1 when the two clustering results are identical [ 27 ]. This metric is used to evaluate whether clustering results based on reduced-dimension similarity are similar to one another. (https://doi.org/10.1016/B978-0-12-805394-2.00015-5)

gap_stat <- clusGap(base_numerica, FUN =factoextra::hcut, K.max = 7)

Interest rates

Many indices have been proposed in the literature to determine the optimal number of clusters in a dataset partition during the clustering process.

The NbClust package, published by Charrad et al. (2014), provides 30 indices for determining the appropriate number of clusters and suggests the best clustering scheme to users based on results obtained by varying all combinations of cluster counts, distance measures, and clustering methods.

The indices provided in the NbClust package include the gap statistic, the silhouette method, and 28 other indices described in detail in the original article by Charrad et al. (2014).

You have to convert it to numeric—that’s fine, since you specify binary distance.

It doesn’t work for our needs, though it could be done.

set.seed(123)
memory.limit(size=1e+13)
## Warning: 'memory.limit()' is no longer supported
## [1] Inf
res.nb <- NbClust::NbClust(data = apply(myMMcondition[,-1], 2, function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x))),
                           diss = NULL,
                  distance = "binary",
                  min.nc = 1, max.nc = 7, method = 'complete', index = "all")
## Warning in sequence.default(n..1, from = seq.int(s.1, length(df), s.1), : NAs

                   method = "complete", index="silhouette")
